To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the curvature perturbation on a sufficiently large comving scale is conserved if the pressure is a function of the energy only, and if the universe is smooth on a sufficiently large scale.
the curvature perturbation on comoving surfaces is conserved provided the pressure is a single-valued function of the energy.

(a) the curvature perturbation on comoving slices is conserved provided the pressure is a function of the density, (b) this conservation holds even if there are non-adiabatic perturbations, (c) the curvature perturbations on uniform-density slices is also conserved provided the density is a function of pressure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the behaviour of the curvature perturbations, which is a key ingredient in the theory of cosmology.
the behaviour of the curvature perturbations in a smooth universe, and we show that it is well-defined and conserved under the assumption that the pressure is only a function of the energy-density.
a new approach to perturbation theory, in which we consider the behaviour of the curvature perturbations on a scale which is much larger than the Hubble radius.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the conservation of the cosmological curvature is a consequence of the smoothness assumption, and of the assumption that the pressure is uniquely determined by the energy density.
the curvature perturbation, defined as above, is conserved in a smooth universe, provided that the pressure depends only on the density.
the curvature perturbation on a comoving surface is conserved provided there is no entropy production.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the curvature perturbation, which is a gauge-invariant quantity defined at second order, is conserved at second order, and the conservation equation is the same as that in linear perturbation, provided that the pressure of the universe is a unique function only of the energy density.
the curvature perturbation, as defined, is conserved in the case of a smooth background.

the curvature perturbation on comoving slices is constant on superhorizon scales, and is conserved on subhorizon scales, provided that the pressure and energy density are related by an equation of state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in a smooth universe, the curvature perturbations can be defined without reference to a background, or to a perturbative scheme.

the curvature perturbation can be defined and studied in a way that avoids the need for perturbations to be small, and that the conservation of the perturbation is a robust result which holds even when the pressure is not a unique function of energy density.
the conservation of the cosmological curvature can be understood in terms of general properties of the spacetime, without invoking any specific theory of cosmological perturbations.
